name: Chanarin-Dorfman syndrome
aliases: neutral lipid storage disease with ichthyosis

clinicalPearls: A rare autosomal recessive disorder combining a non-bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma with systemic lipid accumulation
Caused by biallelic variants in ABHD5 (CGI-58), which activates adipose triglyceride lipase, so neutral lipid droplets accumulate in multiple tissues
The diagnostic hallmark is the Jordans anomaly: cytoplasmic lipid vacuoles seen within neutrophils and other leucocytes on a peripheral blood film
Fine white scaling is present from birth, often with a collodion-like presentation, over a background of erythroderma
Multisystem involvement is common, including hepatic steatosis and hepatomegaly, myopathy, sensorineural hearing loss, cataract, and neurological features
Confirm with blood-film examination for vacuolated leucocytes followed by molecular testing of ABHD5
Management is supportive with emollients and gentle keratolytics for the skin plus monitoring and treatment of hepatic and other systemic complications
reference.pathophysiology: Chanarin-Dorfman syndrome arises from loss-of-function variants in ABHD5, which encodes the co-activator protein CGI-58 that normally stimulates adipose triglyceride lipase. When this co-activator is deficient, triglycerides cannot be efficiently hydrolysed and neutral lipid droplets accumulate within the cytoplasm of many cell types, including keratinocytes, hepatocytes, myocytes and circulating leucocytes. In the epidermis, disordered lipid metabolism disrupts the lamellar barrier of the stratum corneum and produces an ichthyosiform erythroderma, while lipid storage elsewhere accounts for hepatic steatosis, myopathy and the characteristic vacuolated leucocytes.
additionalDifferentials: Non-bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma from other transglutaminase or lipoxygenase defects
Multisystem triglyceride storage disease without ichthyosis (NLSDM, PNPLA2)
additionalInvestigations: Peripheral blood film for Jordans anomaly (lipid vacuoles in neutrophils and monocytes)
Liver function tests and hepatic ultrasound for steatosis and hepatomegaly
Creatine kinase and, if indicated, muscle assessment for myopathy
Audiometry and ophthalmological review for hearing loss and cataract
Skin biopsy showing lipid droplets within epidermal and other cells
redFlags: Progressive hepatic dysfunction or cirrhosis developing from chronic steatosis
Marked collodion presentation in the neonate with fluid, electrolyte and temperature instability
Rising creatine kinase or clinical myopathy suggesting significant muscle involvement
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss or visual impairment
reference.prognosis: The ichthyosis is lifelong but generally manageable; prognosis is chiefly determined by systemic organ involvement, particularly the risk of progressive liver disease, and by myopathic, auditory and neurological complications.
pitfalls: Labelling the child as simple congenital ichthyosis and never examining a blood film for Jordans anomaly
Overlooking hepatic steatosis, which can progress silently to fibrosis
Attributing raised creatine kinase to another cause and missing the lipid myopathy
Assuming skin-directed therapy alone is sufficient without multisystem surveillance
management: Manage the ichthyosis with intensive skin care using emollients, keratolytic agents such as urea or lactic acid preparations, and topical retinoids for scaling
Trial a low-fat diet with medium-chain triglyceride substitution, which may reduce lipid accumulation and improve the dermatological and hepatic features
Monitor liver involvement with regular liver function tests and hepatic imaging for steatosis, and avoid additional hepatotoxic insults such as alcohol
Monitor for myopathy with creatine kinase and functional assessment, and screen periodically with audiometry and ophthalmological review for sensorineural hearing loss and cataract
Provide multidisciplinary care coordinating dermatology, hepatology, neurology, audiology and ophthalmology
Offer genetic counselling and family screening given the autosomal recessive ABHD5 inheritance, with testing of at-risk relatives
